_readme: Confirmed metric merges, decided one at a time with the user and recorded here.
Metric ids are the handbook's own row labels turned into slugs, so the same concept
arrives under several ids: a plural 's', a leading sub-item '(a)', or simply a
different table for life and general business. Merging them is a judgement about
what the concept IS, so each entry carries its evidence and the date it was agreed.
A merge is only made after checking the members never occupy the same
(insurer, year, line of business, class of business) slot. Zero overlap means the
ids are complementary halves of one metric and nothing is lost or double counted;
any overlap would mean they are genuinely different things.
Applied in memory, like the insurer aliases, because production restores its
database from the Litestream replica and never sees a local migration.

aliases.label: Interest, Dividend & Rent - Gross
why: One concept, gross investment income, arriving under three ids:
interest_dividend_rent_gross__inr     1,445 rows  'Interest, Dividend & Rent - Gross (Rs Crore)'
a_interest_dividends_rent_gross__inr    483 rows  '(a) Interest, Dividends & Rent - Gross (Rs Lakh)'  [life tables]
a_interest_dividend_rent_gross__inr     420 rows  '(a) Interest, Dividend & Rent - Gross (Rs Crore)'  [shareholders account]
They differ by a plural 's', a sub-item '(a)', and which table they came from.
None of that is identity: the sub-item letter is a position in a printed list, and
the life/general split is already carried by insurer_class.
Checked pairwise for collisions - all three pairs have ZERO overlapping
(insurer, year, line of business, class of business) slots, so the merge cannot
double count.
Agreed with the user on 2026-07-30.

aliases.label: Total - Sources of Funds
why: A RENAME, not a merge. The balance sheet prints TOTAL twice - once closing SOURCES
OF FUNDS and once closing APPLICATION OF FUNDS - and extraction numbered the second
occurrence rather than naming either, leaving a metric called simply 'total'.
Evidence, and it is weaker than decision 1's so it is stated plainly:
Structural - read from Table 89, the heading SOURCES OF FUNDS precedes the first
TOTAL and APPLICATION OF FUNDS precedes the second. Decision 1 established that
extraction numbers repeated labels in the order they appear.
Empirical - the two sides differ only by rounding, which is a fingerprint. GIC
2019-20: handbook prints 36819.3756 and 36819.3772; IRIS holds 36819.3756 under
total__inr and 36819.3772 under total_2__inr. Both match exactly.
Verified on one insurer end to end, not the 1,758 cells of decision 1 - a scaled
check was blocked because the handbook writes 'GIC' and the resolver cannot match a
three-letter abbreviation. Accepted anyway because this changes a LABEL and no
value: if the two were ever swapped, the numbers stay correct and only the names
trade places. Agreed with the user on 2026-07-30.

aliases.label: Total - Application of Funds
why: The second TOTAL of the balance sheet. See total_sources_of_funds__inr for the
evidence; the two were established together.

aliases.label: Provisions (other than taxation) - Others
why: 'Others' on its own names nothing. The parent row is what gives it meaning, and the
parent was read directly from the handbook: Table 24 puts '(b) Others' under
'Provisions (other than taxation)' in the Policyholders Account, and Tables 25, 51
and 88 put '(c) Others' under the same parent in the Shareholders Account.
The sub-item letter differs only because the parent sits at a different position in
each statement - it is a place in a printed list, not identity.
Safe to merge: ZERO overlapping (insurer, year, line of business, class of business)
slots, because one lives in the Policyholders Account and the other in the
Shareholders Account, a distinction Line_of_Business already carries.
Agreed with the user on 2026-07-30.

aliases.label: Other Expenses - Others
why: A RENAME, deliberately NOT merged with the Provisions 'Others' above. Table 51 and
Table 88 print '(c) Others' twice in the Shareholders Account - once under PROVISIONS
(Other than taxation) and once under OTHER EXPENSES - and extraction numbered the
second occurrence rather than naming its parent.
The two coexist in 358 (insurer, year, statement) slots, so they are demonstrably
different figures reported side by side; merging would have added two unrelated
amounts together.

aliases.label: Appropriations - Others
why: A RENAME. Table 51 puts '(e) Others' under APPROPRIATIONS in the Shareholders
Account. It coexists with the Provisions 'Others' in 170 slots, so it is a distinct
line item and is kept separate.
